issues.reason: "An appositive has no tense of its own: its typing atom takes the host clause's wrapper — past host -> (Past (Member halvard wheelwright))", and the host clause here is the past "opened".

Measures & units fixes the scale as the surface dimension (stated adjective, else the stated dimension noun — "Record what's said"), and no dimension word appears in "with $2.9-million", so `gross` is an atom no word puts there.
Names and casing makes both halves mandatory for every proper noun, work titles included — "Neither part is optional" — so the named show must have a symbol and exactly one Name fact.

gaps_confirmed: A proper-noun modifier in a noun-noun compound ("American Idol winner") — the compound rules cover common-noun and adjective modifiers only, and a name may not absorb an adjacent lowercase head noun, so the winner-of-the-show relation has no carrier.
A chart-rank adjunct on an event ("opened at No. 11") — Ordinal is defined for an entity's rank in an NP, not for a rank-position PP.
A bare money amount as an accompaniment ("with $2.9-million") — no dimension word is stated, so Measure has no licensed scale.
A title noun premodifying a name ("winner Kelly Clarkson") under a past host — whether the appositive tense-wrapper reaches it is unstated.
new_gaps: The participial reduced relative "starring …" gets no tense of its own; the instruction set fixes the tense of an appositive typing atom but says nothing about a reduced-relative event under a past host.
repair_summary: Wrapped the appositive typing atom as (Past (Member from_justin_to_kelly romance)); added (Name american_idol "American Idol") for the dropped proper noun; removed the invented-scale (Measure sk_open_1 gross 2900000 dollar) atom.
notes: The $2.9-million amount is dropped rather than re-slotted, since no stated dimension licenses a Measure and inventing one is barred. Ordinal for "at No. 11" is graceful improvisation in gap territory — true and well-typed — so it stands, as do kc_kind and jg_kind, which no confirmed issue names.
